correctness.rationale: The tail ODE follows exactly by summing the normalized Cao–Gong birth-death equations; its Jacobian is Metzler on the invariant order simplex and strictly compares any distribution ordered relative to the uniform equilibrium. The explicit positive polynomial w_j=j(m+1-j) satisfies (-H)w=1 and gives componentwise strict upper and lower barriers with derivative signs valid for all m=2k>=4. Their monotone bounded orbits converge, and the geometric stationary-flux equation has precisely three equilibria. The ordered solution is consequently squeezed to the appropriate extreme. At uniform the symmetric tail Jacobian H+2/[m(m+1)]11^T has inertia (1 positive,m-1 negative) from alpha*1^T(-H)^-1 1=(m+2)/3>1. The standard-library reproducibility script passed 30 exact signed configurations and two example trajectories; these finite checks are not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The May 27, 2026 primary source derives the exact nonlinear opinion model and characterizes all three equilibria, but proves only symmetry-invariant uniform convergence and extreme-mean sufficient basins. The new globally sufficient first-order stochastic-order criterion covers nonsymmetric moderate-mean cases outside those conclusions, and the full uniform-equilibrium Jacobian inertia is not determined in the cited results. Standard Kamke comparison and stable-manifold theory are classical; the explicit ordered-tail representation and strict polynomial barriers provide the missing model-specific hypotheses and global selection proof. No directly equivalent claim was located in searched research records and literature; unindexed equivalences remain possible.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent stochastic-order comparison theorem for the same incremental-voter ODE might exist in literature outside the examined records.
Abstract-only comparisons for two related opinion-model papers cannot exclude every result in those full texts, although their stated models differ.
The global selection statement is only sufficient and leaves incomparable initial distributions open.

value.rationale: The motivating article identifies the nonsymmetric consensus-selection problem as open beyond its extreme-mean sufficient bounds. The order certificate consists of natural, interpretable cumulative-probability inequalities, applies to a positive-dimensional family for every k>=2, and specifically resolves two moderate-mean five-opinion examples previously outside proved regions. The one-dimensional instability index describes the geometry of the uniform threshold and why exceptional symmetric data may converge there. This supplies motivated structure rather than a routine restatement or a single arbitrary example.
